name: BROCKMAN, William (Slade) Edward Slade

headline.note: Named Ideas Department management role in 1996–1998 added. Australian Grains Champion corrected to private commercial company work, distinct from PGA association and political staff. Hours, leave and early business chronology remain unresolved; no headline years calculated.

career_spells.evidence_note: Brockman and party biographies report running or working on the family farm; a detailed secondary profile says he returned after study and worked as a labourer and manager until 1996. Commencement, entity, ownership, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Agricultural work is supported, but its start, employment relationship and substantive full-time duration are not established.

career_spells.evidence_note: Party biographies refer generally to management roles in business, and a secondary profile places operations/general-manager work after 1996. Employer names, role boundaries, hours, leave and the 2005 transition are not published. Follow-up identifies Ideas Department 1996–1998 within this umbrella. Remaining businesses and 1998–2005 allocation unresolved; umbrella must not be added to individual roles.
career_spells.counting_note: The evidence is too non-specific to count a private full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: Pastoralists and Graziers Association of Western Australia
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography records 2005-08. Parliamentary inquiry evidence and a 2008 PGA submission contemporaneously identify Brockman as policy director, and his first speech describes his wheat-market work. Exact boundaries, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Industry-association employment is excluded from the public/private headline under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Senior adviser and chief of staff
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography gives 2008-16. Brockman's first speech and Cormann's valedictory corroborate the appointment, with Cormann specifying chief-of-staff service mainly during opposition. Exact title changes, employment instruments, leave and cessation are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff work is excluded from the headline calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography records the campaign-director role in 2016-17. The WA Parliament's joint-sitting debate contemporaneously notes his work for the grain campaign. Entity, remuneration, hours, leave and exact cessation are not published. Corporate legal adviser and contemporary ABC company-director interview identify a private commercial bidder, correcting the earlier industry-association inference. Official personal role dates 2016–2017 retained; bid events are not personal employment boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Commercial company role is potentially private employment, but paid relationship, substantive full-time status, leave and exact dates remain unproved. No duration counted.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists O'Connor divisional, state-council, federal-council, campaign and Senate-candidate positions from 2008 to 2017. No paid party employment is established. Exact Senate appointment day removed as unsupported party cessation proxy.
career_spells.counting_note: Party and candidate activity is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography and WA joint-sitting record establish appointment to the Senate on 16 August 2017, followed by elections in 2019 and 2025.
Public professional profile identifies company, title and years, Perth/Sydney. Nested within the broad 1996–2005 business period. Legal employer name, hours, leave and contract dates remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

research_notes: Identify all family-farm and private-business entities, exact roles and dates before 2005; resolve study overlap and whether farm work was paid employment, self-employment or family contribution.
Obtain exact appointment/cessation, hours and leave for PGA, Cormann-office and Australian Grains Champion roles, including title changes within the political-staff interval.
Identify the legal entity and paid status of Australian Grains Champion and distinguish industry advocacy from party campaigning.
Resolve leave and cessation arrangements around Liberal preselection and the 16 August 2017 Senate appointment.

Follow-up 2026-10-02: public profile names Ideas Department operations/general management 1996–1998. Search index also exposes 1998–2002 Perth but not the associated employer/title; do not guess. Broader business chronology remains incomplete.

AGC legal adviser identifies Pty Ltd commercial bidder; ABC contemporaneous director interview corroborates private acquisition purpose. Corrected prior association exclusion. Identify payroll/contract, hours and 2017 cessation separately from 2016 bid withdrawal.

Attempted public professional-profile queries, member career interview, Advoc8 and corporate/annual-report leads. LinkedIn 999 and some primary pages 403/Internal Error were source gaps; public index used without authentication or paywall bypass. Next leads: complete public CV or historical employer material for 1998–2005 and contracts for farm/Ideas/AGC.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: targeted exact-year and title searches across the public LinkedIn index, Advoc8, official parliamentary records, Australian Grains Champion materials and contemporary reporting yielded no defensible employer/title for the still-hidden 1998–2002 profile entry and no personal AGC contract or cessation boundary. The apparent 1998–2002 search fragments were unrelated people/events and were not adopted. Remaining leads require a complete public CV, historical employer archive or contract/payroll evidence.
